analyst.summary: Syngene had a rough FY26 -- revenue grew just 3% and profit (before one-offs) fell 20%, mainly because its single largest biologics client cut orders sharply and the company took on new-capacity costs and a forex hit ahead of revenue. The balance sheet, however, remains in excellent shape (very low debt, strong interest cover), and the company just extended a marquee long-term contract with Bristol Myers Squibb out to 2035, suggesting the core client franchise is intact. Management is guiding FY27 as a turnaround year, though its own guidance is only for flattish revenue with margins holding steady, not a sharp rebound, and the stock is not cheap on current earnings. Recommendation: Hold the existing position through this cyclical trough; this is not a call to add, and we would revisit if the client-driven weakness persists past FY27H1 guidance.
